Perform emergency coronary angiography Emergency coronary angiography confirmed near-complete occlusion of the right coronary artery, which was successfully treated with stent implantation. There was diffuse stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending branch, measuring 60% at its most severe point. Following the procedure, the ECG results normalized and the Brugada-like pattern resolved (Figure 2). Brugada syndrome1is a genetic disorder associated with variants in theSCN5Agene,2leading to abnormal ion channel function and increased risk of sudden cardiac death. In contrast, Brugada phenocopies can be induced by reversible conditions, such as myocardial ischemia,3,4pulmonary embolism, electrolyte imbalances, or drug effects.5In this case, the patient had no electrolyte imbalance or pulmonary embolism.
